name: team_planning_funding
description: Get which budget lines each position, filled or open, in a scenario of a Team Planning plan the caller is in draws on. A position draws on the most specific line that matches it: the line's cost_centre is the position's (as team_planning_cost resolves it), its period overlaps the days the position is held, and each of role, level and location the line states is the position's (location is an occupant's country, else that of the person it replaces). A line with no cost centre matches any position and is the least specific; past that, the more of role, level and location a line states, the more specific. The budget_strictness rule, given as strictness, names the dimensions that must match (match): one outside it no longer blocks a line, a line whose stated dimensions agree outranks one where they differ, and its default, position_control, holds all four. Each draw lists differs_on, the dimensions its line states that the position doesn't share, and variance, those the rule holds, which someone must approve; a difference outside it is a record of the trade. source is 'derived', or 'set' by team_planning_set_position_funding, which wins. A position is unfunded with a reason: no_line, ambiguous (matching_ids lists the lines that tie; none is picked) or line_gone (its funding names a line the scenario no longer holds). Each line lists its positions in draw order, filled first, then open positions replacing a leaver, then other open positions, each by starts_on then id, with draw_reason saying which. Totals count positions and FTE: funded counts the positions funded whole and the FTE every draw funds, each position at its whole FTE, and funded plus unfunded is always the total, over the positions team_planning_cost reads. A set funding is taken as given, whatever the line. FTE and shares are decimal strings. The baseline has no period, so it can't be the scenario. An archived plan carries archived_on, priced_on and a note: its figures use the pay bands, exchange rates, budget lines and rules as they stood on priced_on, its archive day, while framework roles and levels are read as they are now. A plan archived before that copy was kept, or read where its copy can't be opened, has no priced_on, and its figures use today's. Restoring a plan prices it with today's again. Refused, as an unknown plan, unless the caller is a member.

scenario_id.description: A scenario of the plan; not the plan's id, as the baseline has no period.
